name: stri_pad_left
title: Pad a string on the left

origin.description: Add pad characters on the left until each string reaches width.
origin.usage: stri_pad_left(str, width = floor(0.9 * getOption("width")), pad = " ", use_length = FALSE)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Minimum output widths. The default is floor(0.9 * getOption("width")), which is 72 under Rscript.

arguments.name: pad
arguments.text: Padding text. Its display width must be 1, or it must be one code point when use_length is TRUE.

arguments.name: use_length
arguments.text: TRUE counts code points. FALSE, the default, counts display width.

origin.details: Vectorized over str, width, and pad. Width is the display width from stri_width unless use_length is TRUE. A string that is already wide enough is unchanged. A missing string, width, or pad yields a missing result.
origin.example:
x <- stri_pad_left("stringi", 10, pad = "#")
cat(paste0('stri_pad_left("stringi", 10, "#") returns ', x, '.\n'))

translation.description: Add pad characters on the left until each string reaches width.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Minimum output widths. The default is floor(0.9 * getOption("width")), which is 72 under Rscript.

arguments.name: pad
arguments.text: Padding text. Its display width must be 1, or it must be one code point when use_length is TRUE.

arguments.name: use_length
arguments.text: TRUE counts code points. FALSE, the default, counts display width.

translation.details: Display width comes from stri_width. use_length TRUE counts code points instead, and then pad must be exactly one code point. A string that is already wide enough is unchanged. A missing string, width, or pad yields NA. The default width is 72.
translation.value: A string, or NA. A list returns a list. None returns an empty list.
translation.example:
from stringi.pad import stri_pad_left
x = stri_pad_left("stringi", 10, pad="#")
print(f'stri_pad_left("stringi", 10, "#") returns {x}.')
